errors.description: Model incorrectly assumed the arrow moved directly from orange to purple, skipping white, which contradicts the actual sequence of events (orange → white → purple).
errors.evidence_quote: Model trace: 'The arrow starts at the left-side orange square... and moves toward the right-side purple square.'

errors.description: Model incorrectly inferred that the orange-to-purple segment was the shortest in time, when in fact the orange-to-white segment took only 0.50s — the shortest duration — and white-to-purple took 1.00s.

analysis_result.analysis: The model fundamentally misordered the trajectory of the arrow, incorrectly assuming a direct path from orange to purple while ignoring the intermediate white shape. This led to a false conclusion about which segment took the shortest time. The ground truth clearly shows the arrow moves orange → white (0.50s) → purple (1.00s), making white the correct answer. The model’s reasoning conflates spatial distance with temporal duration and fails to track the actual sequence of events, resulting in a major temporal and grounding error.
